edits.old: The sheet gives no iron setting for the eight 0201 parts: open, for the lead.
edits.new: The process sheet gives no iron setting for the eight 0201 parts (its hand soldering table, `design/mfg/assembly/process.md:148` to `design/mfg/assembly/process.md:155`, has no row for them), and the board may not go back through the oven to put a part right (`design/mfg/assembly/process.md:116`: "No third reflow of the ring board, ever"): the iron setting for these parts is open, for the lead.

edits.old: the red lead to the + land and the blue lead to the - land, by hand soldering
edits.new: the red lead to the + land and the minus lead to the - land, by hand soldering. The minus lead is black on some motors and blue on others: the maker's drawing gives it as "Black or Blue" (`design/ecad/band/band-interface.md:122`); either colour goes on the - land

edits.old: J_BAND_A at the upper left, beside the engraving "A FLEX1". The board lies flat and flush and does not rock.
edits.new: J_BAND_A at the upper left, beside the engraving "A FLEX1". The board lies flat and flush and does not rock. The board carries no printing, so tell the two land groups apart by their lands, at 10 times: J_BAND_A has 8 lands, two full rows of 4; J_BAND_B has 7 lands, and its row nearer the board edge has only 3, with the empty place at the right end (+X, the fingertip end) (`design/ecad/band/band-interface.md:30` to `design/ecad/band/band-interface.md:52`). Both groups lie left of the board's middle; J_BAND_A is on the upper edge and J_BAND_B on the lower edge, the same edge as the antenna ANT1, the 3.2 x 1.6 mm chip at the lower left corner (ANT1 at X -10.80, Y 5.25, step 2). If the 7-land group is at the top, the board lies the wrong way round: lift it out, turn it and lay it in again.

edits.new: SW1 terminal 4 to C28 pad 2 beeps (the ground pair A6 and A8: the beep proves that at least one of the two is joined, not each one).

edits.new: this proves lands B4, B5 and B6, and the ground pair B2 and B7 once more as a pair.

edits.old: What the meter cannot see: lands A6 and A8 are both ground and joined on the ribbon, so one open of the two reads as good; only an X-ray of the joint shows it, and the lead decides whether it is asked (`design/mfg/assembly/hotbar-joint.md:184`).
edits.new: The ground lands, what the checks prove: each ribbon has two ground lands that the ribbon's own copper joins, A6 and A8 on FLEX1 and B2 and B7 on FLEX2, so one open land of a pair reads as good on every check above. By the lead's decision they are a redundant pair: the design needs at least one joint of each pair, the meter checks above prove each PAIR and not each land, and no X-ray is asked (`design/wiring/lead-decisions.md:89`). What the eye proves of each of the 15 lands: before the press, its own smooth solder dome and no bridge (How 2); after the press, nothing of the land itself, because every board land lies wholly under the foot (the lands reach 0.20 mm short of the foot's end and 0.335 mm short of its long edges, Locate). The look of How 7 judges the foot as a whole: flat, no lifted corner, not moved, no solder ball beside it. Through the foot, at most a 0.125 mm end of a board land could show, and only where no ribbon copper lies over it: one end of each of A1, A2, A3, A6, B1, B2, B3 and B7 is free of ribbon copper; both ends of A4, A5, A7, A8, B4, B5 and B6 lie under ribbon copper at every size, so these 7 lands cannot be seen at all after the press. No file says that the coverlay and the 0.10 mm stiffener let light through, so even the free ends are not proven visible (`design/mfg/assembly/hotbar-joint.md:184`).
